examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit at Positive or Negative Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
examples.worked_solution:
In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\dfrac{\infty}{\infty},$ so applying  L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\eqalign{
\lim_{x\to \infty}  \dfrac {x^6}{5x^6-4} &= \lim_{x\to\infty}  \dfrac {[x^6]'}{[5x^6-4]'}\
&= \lim_{x\to \infty}  \dfrac {6x^5}{5(6x^5)-0}\
&=  \lim_{x\to \infty}  \dfrac {1}{5}\
&= \dfrac{1}{5}.
}
$$

Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are  ${lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-\infty $ and  ${lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{-\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)]}^{′}}{{[\operatorname{sec}⁡x]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{\cancel{-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cancel{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}(-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}) \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
